proof_summary: Using \(4\cos^2\theta=2+2\cos(2\theta)\), product-to-sum identities, and reduction of angles modulo \(2\pi\), the proof recursively expresses the six elementary symmetric sums of the proposed roots in terms of \(\sum_{j=1}^6\cos(2j\pi/13)\). A telescoping sine identity gives this sum as \(-\tfrac12\), yielding the symmetric sums \(11,45,84,70,21,1\), after which expansion of the product gives the result.
